literal: And further, attachment of what use indeed, for those who have undertaken the severing of birth, even the body is an excess.
translation: For those who have resolved to sever the cycle of birth, even their own body is a superfluous burden; what use, then, are any other attachments?
modern: பிறவிச் சுழற்சியை அறுக்க முயன்றவர்களுக்குத் தமது உடம்பே ஒரு சுமையாகும் போது, வேறு பிற பற்றுகள் எதற்காக?
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute nature of renunciation. For those who have committed to ending the cycle of birth and death, even their own physical body is seen as an extra, unnecessary burden. If the very body they inhabit is considered superfluous to their spiritual goal, then any other worldly attachments are completely useless. The author uses this stark comparison to show that true renunciation requires letting go of all external bonds, as even the physical self is ultimately a temporary vessel to be transcended.
